output.brief:
The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14. A new Corvane rule (AUTO-LIB-17) arrived in the 3 March vendor rule-pack update, activated at 10:38 UTC. It blocks password logins from the app's networking library when no edge session cookie is present. The first block was at 10:41, and the telemetry shows failures starting on every app version within a minute. About 41,000 blocked installs, 92% with a recent successful login, are real customers, not bots. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. The failures don't depend on app version or on the OS security patch. The origin's error rates are unchanged, so the auth-service change is not implicated. Rolling back 6.14 would not help. Neither would tightening bot protection, which would block more customers. Excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would hide a real customer problem.
Next: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password-login path, keeping the other protections. Then confirm in telemetry that password-login success returns to about 96%. Keep the 6.14 rollout going and watch outcomes by version. Ask Corvane to give notice of rule changes in future. I'm fairly confident. The call-volume link is plausible but confounded by the fee notices.
